indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.1.2.1 Recognise materials as important resources for providing human needs
indicator.objective: Know the general properties of metals such as lustre, malleability, conductivity and ductility

skills.description: Explain lustre as the shiny appearance of metals.
Explain malleability as the ability of metals to be hammered or pressed into thin sheets without breaking.
Explain conductivity as the ability of metals to carry heat or electricity.
Explain ductility as the ability of metals to be drawn into thin wires.
Identify which property is shown by a given example (e.g. copper wire → ductility; aluminium foil → malleability).
Classify materials as metals or non-metals based on these properties.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Metals cannot be bent or shaped.
Ductility and malleability are the same thing.
Plastic is a metal because it can be shaped.
Lustre means a material is heavy.

questions.stem: What is lustre?
hints: Think about how shiny a new coin looks.
questions.explanation: Lustre is the shiny appearance of metals.
questions.misconception: Lustre means a material is heavy.

questions.stem: Which of these best describes lustre?
options: The ability of a metal to be drawn into wires
The shiny appearance of a metal
The ability of a metal to conduct electricity
The ability of a metal to be hammered into sheets
hints: It is about how shiny the metal looks.
questions.explanation: Lustre is the shiny appearance of a metal.
questions.misconception: Lustre means ductility.

questions.stem: What does lustre mean when describing a metal?
questions.explanation: Lustre means the shiny appearance of a metal.
questions.misconception: Lustre means weight.

questions.stem: What is malleability?
options: The ability of a metal to be hammered into thin sheets
The ability of a metal to be drawn into wires
The shiny appearance of a metal
The ability of a metal to conduct heat
questions.explanation: Malleability is the ability of a metal to be hammered or pressed into thin sheets without breaking.
questions.misconception: Malleability means ductility.

questions.stem: Which property allows a metal to be hammered into a flat sheet?
questions.explanation: Malleability is the property that allows a metal to be hammered or pressed into thin sheets.
questions.misconception: Ductility allows metals to be hammered into sheets.

questions.stem: What is malleability?
answer: the ability of a metal to be hammered or pressed into thin sheets
the ability of a metal to be shaped into thin sheets
metals can be hammered into flat sheets
hints: It can be made into sheets.
questions.explanation: Malleability is the ability of a metal to be hammered or pressed into thin sheets without breaking.
questions.misconception: Malleability and ductility are the same.

questions.stem: A metalsmith hammers a piece of gold into a very thin sheet. Which property of metals does this show?
hints: The metal is being made into a sheet.
It is not being drawn into a wire.
questions.explanation: Hammering gold into a thin sheet shows malleability.
questions.misconception: Hammering into sheets shows ductility.

questions.stem: What is conductivity in metals?
options: The ability to carry heat or electricity
The ability to be hammered into sheets
The ability to be drawn into wires
hints: Think about how wires carry electricity.
Metals can pass heat and electricity.
questions.explanation: Conductivity is the ability of metals to carry heat or electricity.
questions.misconception: Conductivity is about shininess.

questions.stem: Which property allows copper to be used for electrical wires?
questions.explanation: Copper is used for electrical wires because of its conductivity — it can carry electricity.
questions.misconception: Copper is used for wires because it is shiny.

questions.stem: What is conductivity?
answer: the ability of a metal to carry heat or electricity
the ability to conduct electricity or heat
hints: Think about metal pots on fire.
questions.explanation: Conductivity is the ability of metals to carry heat or electricity.
questions.misconception: Conductivity means shininess.

questions.stem: Why are cooking pots made of metals?
hints: Pots need to get hot on the fire.
questions.explanation: Cooking pots are made of metals because metals conduct heat, allowing food to cook evenly.
questions.misconception: Pots are made of metals because they are shiny.

questions.stem: What is ductility?
options: The ability of a metal to be drawn into thin wires
The ability of a metal to be hammered into sheets
The shiny appearance of a metal
The ability of a metal to carry heat
questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability of a metal to be drawn into thin wires.
questions.misconception: Ductility means being hammered into sheets.

questions.stem: Which property allows copper to be drawn into thin wires?
questions.explanation: Ductility is the property that allows copper to be drawn into thin wires.
questions.misconception: Malleability allows metals to be drawn into wires.

questions.stem: What is ductility?
answer: the ability of a metal to be drawn into thin wires
metals can be drawn into wires
the ability to be made into wires
questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability of a metal to be drawn into thin wires.
questions.misconception: Ductility and malleability are the same.

questions.stem: A copper wire is used in a circuit. Which property of copper is being used?
hints: Which property allows electricity to flow?
questions.explanation: The copper wire carries electricity, showing the conductivity of copper.
questions.misconception: Copper wire works because of lustre.

questions.stem: Aluminium foil is used to wrap food. It can be pressed into a thin sheet. Which property does aluminium show?
hints: The metal is pressed into a sheet.
questions.explanation: Aluminium foil shows malleability because it is pressed into a thin sheet.
questions.misconception: Aluminium foil shows ductility.

questions.stem: A pupil observes that a metal spoon shines in the light. Which property of metals is this?
questions.explanation: The shiny appearance of the metal spoon is lustre.
questions.misconception: Shininess is conductivity.

questions.stem: A pupil stretches a piece of copper into a thin wire and hammers another piece into a flat sheet. Which two properties are shown?
questions.explanation: Drawing copper into a wire shows ductility. Hammering copper into a sheet shows malleability.
questions.misconception: Ductility and malleability are the same.

questions.stem: A pupil tests four materials by trying to hammer them into sheets. Which material is a metal?
hints: Which material can be shaped by hammering?
questions.explanation: A copper coin is a metal and is malleable. Plastic, chalk and rubber are not metals.
questions.misconception: Plastic is a metal.

questions.stem: A pupil has a metal nail and a plastic spoon. Which one conducts electricity? Explain your answer.
answer: the metal nail conducts electricity because it is a metal
the nail conducts electricity; plastic does not
the metal nail, because metals are conductors
questions.explanation: The metal nail conducts electricity because metals have conductivity. The plastic spoon is an insulator and does not conduct.
questions.misconception: Plastic is a conductor.
